hooks.command: : 'Hammerspoon card when Claude needs attention (permission prompt, idle input)'; "$HOME/bin/claude-notify.sh"
: 'Hammerspoon card with chat title, repo/branch and the start of the last reply'; "$HOME/bin/claude-notify.sh"

: 'Terminal bell on finish. Hooks have no tty, so write to the parent (Claude) tty; tr strips the space ps adds'; tty=$(ps -o tty= -p $PPID | tr -d ' '); [ -n "$tty" ] && [ "$tty" != "??" ] && printf '\a' > "/dev/$tty"; exit 0

statusLine.command: if command -v ccstatusline >/dev/null 2>&1; then ccstatusline; else echo 'ccstatusline not installed: bun add -g ccstatusline@2.2.32'; fi

environment: **Internal sharing / snippet hosting**: None configured — treat public paste/gist services as outside the trust boundary
**Default / protected branches**: Default branch is `master`; no rulesets or protected branches listed (via gh)
**Host containment**: None configured — assume Claude Code runs on an ordinary developer machine or CI runner with open internet
**Source control**: The trusted repo (github.com:edwardbaeg/dotfiles.git) only — no additional orgs configured

**Sensitive data locations & audiences**: any file or store holding personal data, confidential business data, credentials, regulated data, or similarly sensitive material; preserve exact handles when known and share only with audiences cleared at the [named+specifics] bar — note: `.env.example` is a template with empty values, not itself sensitive, but treat any real `.env` in this repo as sensitive
**Sensitive remote targets**: any namespace, host, or container whose name carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment
**Protected deployment namespaces / environments**: None configured — fall back to the Sensitive remote targets heuristic
**Protected IaC scopes**: IAM, RBAC, networking, quota, and node-pool resources; anything whose name or tag carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment
**Primary use of Claude Code**: software development (personal dotfiles management — neovim, terminal, shell configuration)

**Trusted repo**: github.com:edwardbaeg/dotfiles.git (public) — this repo is public, so only this repo's own work is fine to push there; confidential material or secrets are never cleared into it by virtue of visibility
Routine actions under this repo's own paths (stow targets, Makefile targets like stow-*, lint, test) are routine for this project
